match.reason: The closest bank point, economic and financial influences, covers how general conditions affect spending and costs, but it does not teach how the global economic outlook, world funds and international interest rates affect the cost and availability of finance at Year 12 depth.

draft.title: Global market influences
card: Australian businesses do not borrow in a closed market. Conditions overseas can change what finance costs and whether it can be had.
World economic outlook
when the world economy is strong, lenders and investors are more willing to supply funds. When it looks weak or uncertain, they may hold back or ask for higher returns.
Availability of funds
Australian banks and companies often borrow from overseas lenders. If those lenders cut back, less finance is on offer here and it can cost more.
Global interest rates
when rates rise overseas, Australian lenders may pay more for the funds they borrow abroad, and may pass that on as higher rates to business borrowers.
draft.remember: Conditions overseas can change the cost and supply of finance for an Australian business.

a.q: Why can a rise in interest rates overseas affect a business borrowing in Australia?
opts: Lenders may pay more for overseas funds and pass it on
Australian law then sets the business's loan rate overseas
The business must then repay all its loans in full at once
Overseas lenders then take over the business's local bank
a.why: Australian lenders often raise some of their funds overseas. If those funds cost more, lenders may pass the extra cost on as higher rates. The other options describe things the card does not say happen.
a.clue: Think about where Australian lenders get some of their funds.

b.q: Overseas lenders become nervous about a weak world economy and lend less to Australian banks. What is the most likely effect on Priya, who wants a business loan in Perth?
opts: Finance may be harder to get and cost more
Finance becomes easier to get and costs less
Her loan is unaffected, as only local conditions count
Her loan is cheaper, because banks have less to lend
b.why: When overseas lenders cut back, less finance is on offer in Australia, so it may be harder to get and cost more. Having less to lend does not make a loan cheaper: scarcer funds tend to cost more.
b.clue: Less money on offer usually means a higher price.

a.best: Lenders may pay more for overseas funds and pass it on

b.best: Finance may be harder to get and cost more

problems.detail: The right option is the only hedged one ('may'). The distractors are absolute or extreme ('must... repay all its loans in full at once', 'take over', 'sets'), so a student could pick the answer from test-taking cues alone.
The right option is the only one with a qualifier ('may'). The distractors use absolutes ('only local conditions count', 'becomes'), so the answer stands out without knowing the idea.

proposal.title: Global market influences
card: Australian businesses do not borrow in a closed market. Conditions overseas can change what finance costs and whether it can be had.
World economic outlook
when the world economy is strong, lenders and investors are more willing to supply funds. When it looks weak or uncertain, they may hold back or ask for higher returns.
Availability of funds
Australian banks and companies often borrow from overseas lenders. If those lenders cut back, less finance is on offer here and it can cost more.
Global interest rates
when rates rise overseas, Australian lenders may pay more for the funds they borrow abroad, and may pass that on as higher rates to business borrowers.
proposal.remember: Conditions overseas can change the cost and supply of finance for an Australian business.

a.q: Why can a rise in interest rates overseas affect a business borrowing in Australia?
opts: Its lender can pay more for the funds it borrows abroad
Its lender can pay less for the funds it borrows abroad
Its lender can lend more as overseas savers move funds here
Its lender can ignore it, as Australia is a closed market
a.why: Australian lenders often raise some of their funds overseas. When rates rise there, those funds can cost more, and lenders may pass that on to business borrowers. Paying less reverses the effect, and the card says Australia is not a closed market.
a.clue: Think about where Australian lenders get some of their funds.

b.q: Overseas lenders become nervous about a weak world economy and lend less to Australian banks. What is the most likely effect on Priya, who wants a business loan in Perth?
opts: Finance is harder to get and costs more
Finance is easier to get and costs less
Finance is harder to get but costs less
Finance is unchanged, as Perth banks lend locally
b.why: When overseas lenders cut back, less finance is on offer in Australia, so it tends to be harder to get and cost more. Scarcer funds do not make a loan cheaper, and Australian banks often rely on overseas funds, so local lending is affected too.
b.clue: Less money on offer usually means a higher price.
